subject: Launch week quota ask and overrun settlement playbook
messages:
From: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@atlascommerce.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary quota uplift and billing path for launch week

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Quick note — our pilot moves to production next Monday and the first 48 hours are expected to spike above our current committed quota. We saw the forecast in staging and expect a 3x ingest/requests profile for ~36 hours, then a taper. Can Redwood temporarily raise our request cap and offer a clear billing path for the overrun?

Specific asks:
- Short-term rate-limit increase from 200 r/s to 1,200 r/s for 48 hours (UTC-7) starting 2026-10-19 00:00.
- A reconciled invoice or credit approach for the overrun (we need a predictable unit charge or an agreed credit).
- Any paperwork required now so procurement can sign before the window.

I attached the usage snapshot from our staging run.

Thanks — Patricia
Patricia Gomez
Head of Ops, Atlas Commerce
patricia.gomez@atlascommerce.com

Attachments: consumption_report_q3_launch.csv (CSV, 78KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@atlascommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quota uplift and billing path for launch week

Patricia —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the consumption snapshot, that helps. We can support a temporary uplift but want to align on pricing and legal steps before the window. Looping Ben to propose the commercial path; looping Laura for any product-side constraints.

Quick Qs for your team so we price the overrun appropriately:
- Is this a hard launch cutover (all traffic flips) or phased? (helps size the uplift)
- Do you have a projected token/request mix during the spike?

We’ll come back with a short playbook (pricing + addendum) within the day.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@atlascommerce.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quota uplift and billing path for launch week

Hi Karthik / Ben —

Quick answers:
- This is a full-traffic cutover over a single weekend; we expect peak load hours starting 2026-10-19 00:00 UTC-7 and most pressure in the first 36 hours.
- Forecast sample: ~4M tokens/hour at peak, ~average 1.2M tokens/hour outside peak. We'll send a detailed token mix before Friday.

Procurement is ready to sign an amendment but needs clear language on overrun charges vs credits. Ideally: a short-term uplift at a defined unit overrun rate or a credit equal to X% off overrun if we commit to a 12-month reserved plan within 30 days.

Can Redwood propose a 48–72 hour uplift with an explicit settlement path we can pre-approve?

Patricia

> On Oct 10, 2026, at 10:03, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> > We’ll come back with a short playbook (pricing + addendum) within the day.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@atlascommerce.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed uplift & overrun settlement (Atlas Commerce)

Patricia —

Thanks for the details. Based on the forecast and a 48–72 hour uplift window, here’s a concise commercial path we can execute quickly:

Proposal (short-term uplift):
- Temporary rate-limit increase to 1,200 r/s for a 72-hour window starting 2026-10-19 00:00 UTC-7.
- During the uplift window, overrun consumption billed at a blended overrun rate of $0.0125 per token (discounted from standard overrun tiers).
- If Atlas signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment within 30 days of the uplift, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 20% of billed overrun for that uplift window. Credit will apply to the first invoice after the commitment becomes active.
- No change to data residency or security posture; standard SOC2 controls remain in place.

Operational items:
- We’ll create a simple amendment (DocuSign link) capturing the window and rate; legal can sign.
- We’ll require a short proof-of-use report after the event (we’ll attach a template).

Attachments: redwood_proposed_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF, 45KB), example_proof_of_use_template.xlsx

If that looks acceptable I’ll open the DocuSign and we can get procurement to sign before the window. Happy to tweak the blended rate or the credit % if procurement needs different economics.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

> On Oct 11, 2026, at 08:47, Patricia Gomez wrote:
> > Procurement is ready to sign an amendment but needs clear language on overrun charges vs credits.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Gomez <pgomez@atlascommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed uplift & overrun settlement (Atlas Commerce)

Patricia —

Ben’s proposal is our recommended path. A couple of clarifications from the product/ops side (Laura):
- We’ll provision the uplift in a pre-authorized config and monitor the headroom. If Atlas approaches the cap earlier than expected we can extend by an hour-by-hour admin toggle, but any extension beyond the 72 hours will default to the standard overrun rate unless we agree otherwise.
- Proof-of-use will be a one-page CSV report (start/end tokens per hour + peak minute).

Next steps:
1) Ben to send DocuSign amendment (captures uplift window + blended rate + credit clause).
2) Patricia / procurement signs and returns before 2026-10-17 EOD.
3) Redwood ops will provision uplift and run a short smoke test on 2026-10-18.

We’ll also create a short mutual action plan so Atlas can keep legal/procurement aligned. Ben — if procurement asks for a slightly higher credit (25%) in exchange for a 14-day signature SLA, is that something you can escalate?

— Karthik

Thanks everyone — procurement accepted the amendment with one ask: if Atlas signs a 12-month commitment within 14 days rather than 30, we’d like the credit bumped to 25% of the uplift billed overrun. They asked us to return the signed DocuSign today.

We’ll sign if Redwood confirms the 25% credit for a 14-day conversion SLA. Otherwise procurement will request the original 30-day / 20% term.

Can Ben confirm final credit and send the DocuSign? Once signed we’ll route to ops for provisioning.

Patricia
